incident-bot: PagerDuty PAGE fired: Billing > usage-metering pipeline high lag (PD#PD12345) - Severity: P1 - paging on-call: Alice K. <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345|PD12345>

Alice K.: acked, starting triage. thanks. I'm on-call for infra now.

pagerduty: Acknowledged by Alice K. at 2026-03-14T14:01:40Z

Ben M.: seeing big consumer lag on usage-processor group. kafka lag ~12k msgs, CPU on usage-agg pods spiking.

Carla S. (billing-eng): FYI we've got token_count deltas showing up between 14:00-15:30 UTC vs expected. Possible undercounting. Finance flagged pending invoices.

David R.: pulling logs now. stack traces show rate-limited 502s from token-count-aggregator to redis cluster. redis latency jump ~120ms.

Ben M.: logs excerpt:
```
ERROR token_count_agg - http 502 from /kv/append - upstream_timeout
kafka-consumer-lag: topic=usage-events partition=4 lag=12345
```

Irene (support): three paying customers opened priority tickets citing invoice mismatch. tagging them in support queue.

Alice K.: immediate questions: is this ingestion lag (lost events) or aggregation mismatch? Ben, can you confirm whether events are sitting in Kafka or dropped?

Ben M.: events are in Kafka, not being processed fast enough. consumer offsets stuck. We can try: 1) bounce consumers on cluster-a, 2) fail traffic to legacy-meter-runner (stateless) to compute counts, 3) start a backfill.

Carla S.: we need to avoid recharging customers incorrectly. Finance requests we PAUSE today's invoice run for affected window until reconciled. I'll coordinate.

David R.: rolling restart consumer group cg-usage-agg on cluster-a now (one pod at a time). command: 
```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/usage-aggregator --field-selector spec.template.metadata.labels.zone=cluster-a
```

Ben M.: starting backfill job bf-987 against topic partition subset to catch up. estimate ~45m. kicking off with lower concurrency to avoid stressing redis.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation set: if not resolved by 14:10 UTC escalate to eng-lead.

Alice K.: handoff - I'm going to step out for a meeting at 14:15 UTC. Ben can take lead for next 30m. @Carla_S please keep finance looped.

Carla S.: Finance: initiating soft-hold on invoice-service for today's hourly batch. cron disabled: 
```
# disable invoice cron
kubectl -n prod patch cronjob/invoice-runner -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```

Irene (support): updating customers and status page: "We are investigating an issue affecting billing token counts for a subset of invoices. We have paused today's batch while we reconcile counts. No double-billing expected"

Ben M.: backfill progress: 20% done - consumer offsets moved forward ~2.5k msgs, redis error rate dropping.

David R.: added a small throttling rule on token-count-aggregator to reduce burst writes to redis: 
```
# temporary rate-limit config
curl -XPATCH https://config-service/internal -d '{"service":"token-count-agg","rate_limit":500}'
```

Carla S.: quick check against ledger: for window 14:00-14:30 UTC, token delta now within 0.4% of expected after backfill partial run. Finance happy to hold invoices until we reach <0.5% diff.

Ben M.: backfill complete for affected partitions. kickstarting a reconcile job to recompute per-customer counts for 14:00-15:30 UTC. job id: reconcile-226.

Irene (support): customer comms sent for the 3 impacted customers + status page note pinned.

Carla S.: reconcile result: majority matched; 12 accounts had small undercounts. I've queued adjustments and will rerun invoices for those accounts once finance signs off.

Alice K.: I'm back. quick status?

Ben M.: root cause likely bursty upstream causing consumer to block and redis timeouts under write pressure. Mitigations: throttling, consumer restarts, backfill. Reconcile done.

Carla S.: Finance approved re-run for affected accounts only. invoice-service cron left suspended for full-day; will re-enable after postmortem and manual verification.

incident-bot: PD#PD12345 marked resolved by Alice K. at 2026-03-14T14:34:10Z

Alice K.: closing the page. Creating follow-up ticket: INF-4578 (billing pipeline hardening + redis scaling + consumer backpressure tests). Owners:
- Ben M. -> consumer resilience & backpressure tests
- David R. -> redis capacity + 99th pct latency dashboards
- Carla S. -> billing reconciliation automation + invoice safe-hold runbook

Irene (support): I'll draft customer-facing post-incident message and coordinate with comms.

Ben M.: quick note for postmortem: reproduce locally with load.py --burst 50k/events/min against usage-processor to validate throttle thresholds.

Alice K.: thanks everyone. we'll do a blameless postmortem and schedule a follow-up next week. :white_check_mark:

Carla S.: tagging incident ticket in product board and finance ledger.

Irene (support): updating incident ticket with list of impacted customers and links to tickets.

Ben M.: closing monitor alerts for this incident. will keep increased alerting sensitivity for 24h.

Alice K.: official status: RESOLVED. follow-ups in INF-4578.
